I could not verify this from the source paper, so this is a low-confidence guess. The most plausible candidate I can reason about is $S = M_{11}$, with $x$ an order-3 automorphism and $r = 11$. Here $|M_{11}| = 2^4\cdot 3^2\cdot 5\cdot 11$, so $r = 11$ divides the order exactly once and is coprime to $|x|=3$. Any subgroup of order divisible by 11 is $M_{11}$ or a copy of $L_2(11)$, so the generation condition is restrictive. This heuristic does not establish that $N = 4$ occurs there.
